model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral mixin for federated identity equivalence: identified, versioned assertions that two externally owned references denote the same subject, carrying issuing authority, applicability, evidence and confidence, without merging, renaming or taking ownership of either endpoint.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 models the alias / same-as assertion as a first-class but weakly identified mixin attached to a host record. It covers the assertion envelope (its own identifier and version, issuer and authorship, assertion and effective times, tenant or adopting Dimension, jurisdiction, purpose and applicable entity/type scope); the endpoint-reference boundary (source and target roles, locator form and namespace or scheme binding, version pins, composite keys, immutable snapshots versus live references, explicit provenance locators and recorded resolution status); the shape of the claim (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many and conditional mappings with explicit membership, ordering and condition guards); the relation-classification slot bound to external predicate vocabularies; the evidence, justification and confidence attached to the claim; the assertion's own lifecycle from proposal through assertion, dispute, supersession, retraction and tombstoning; and the governance that names issuing authority and records conflicts without resolving them. It deliberately holds no power over the things it links: it never allocates or renames an identifier, never edits an endpoint record, and never executes matching, merge, redirect, reasoning closure, authorization or audit.
in_scope: Identity and versioning of the assertion itself, distinct from every identifier cited at its endpoints
Issuer, authorship, review attribution, assertion time, effective window and separately recorded observation or ingestion time
Purpose, tenant or adopting Dimension, jurisdiction, licence and applicable entity/type scope that bound the claim
Source and target role assignment, directionality and the explicit statement of endpoint non-ownership
Endpoint locator form, namespace or scheme binding, compact-form expansion and recorded comparison or normalization level
Endpoint version pins, composite keys, immutable snapshot versus live reference mode and last recorded resolution status
Explicit provenance locators: originating set or linkset, primary source, derivation lineage and issue references
Cardinality of the claim (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many) with explicit membership, combination rule and ordering
Conditional and qualified mappings expressed as attribute-value guards rather than hidden in repeated fields
The relation-classification slot that binds the claim to an external predicate vocabulary, and the evidence, justification and confidence carried with it
The assertion's own lifecycle states and supersession, retraction and tombstone semantics

Degenerate and error states: absence versus explicit unknown versus explicit not-same, dangling and unresolved endpoints, malformed or relative references, self links, duplicate envelopes and conflicting endpoint version pins
out_of_scope: Allocation, minting, naming, formatting, deprecation or non-reuse enforcement of either endpoint identifier
The endpoint records themselves: their attributes, descriptions, labels, classifications and lifecycles
Definition of the predicate vocabularies (owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom, skos:*Match, ConceptMap relationship codes) and their formal semantics
Entailment, transitive closure, equivalence-class computation and any reasoner behaviour over asserted pairs
Record-linkage and matching engine execution: candidate generation, blocking, similarity functions and scoring algorithms
Data merge, survivorship, golden-record construction and master-data consolidation
Dereference, redirect execution, HTTP status handling and resolution-service operation
Authorization decisions, policy evaluation and enforcement
Audit-trail record structure, storage, retention and tamper evidence
Human identity verification, proofing or credential issuance for the subjects at either endpoint

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent owns identifier syntax, scheme and namespace registration, allocation, non-reuse guarantees and reference resolution semantics generally. WM-XCT-036 specializes only the case where two such references are asserted to denote the same subject, and reuses the parent's identifier and resolution machinery by reference rather than restating it.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Endpoint entity and record models at each side of the assertion
boundary_notes.distinction: Those models own the described subjects, their attributes and their lifecycles. This model carries only role-bearing locators, version pins, snapshot digests and recorded resolution observations; it never imports endpoint content and never mutates an endpoint record.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Identifier issuing and registration authority model
boundary_notes.distinction: The issuing authority allocates identifiers, guarantees uniqueness, and decides deprecation and tombstoning of its own identifiers. This model cites that authority and its version tokens; it never allocates, reassigns or retires an endpoint identifier.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Relation classification and semantic predicate vocabularies
boundary_notes.distinction: Vocabulary owners define what owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom, skos:exactMatch, skos:closeMatch and ConceptMap relationship codes mean and entail. This model holds a typed predicate slot that names one such term plus an optional negation modifier; it does not define, extend or reinterpret those terms.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Formal equivalence closure and reasoning model
boundary_notes.distinction: Entailment, transitive closure and equivalence-class materialisation belong to a reasoning model. This model supplies asserted pairs as input and explicitly forbids chaining assertions locally, because skos:closeMatch is deliberately non-transitive while skos:exactMatch is transitive and owl:sameAs propagates to all properties.

The matching engine generates candidates and computes similarity. This model records the resulting justification locator, tool reference and creator-supplied confidence as evidence about a claim; it does not execute, tune or reproduce the scoring.

That model evaluates and enforces access. WM-XCT-036 supplies tenant, jurisdiction, purpose and licence attributes as decision inputs, and separates the DID-style distinction between a subject, a controller and an assertion about a subject; it makes no access decision and stores no decision record.

Assertion creation, supersession, retraction and tombstoning emit events for external capture. Audit-record structure, retention, integrity and query are owned entirely by the audit model; this model stores no audit trail and offers no tamper-evidence guarantee.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Section 9.6 defines individual equality (owl:sameAs) and individual inequality (owl:differentFrom) as assertion axioms, giving the normative distinction between asserting sameness and asserting explicit not-sameness.

sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Syntax
sources.relevance: Requires IRIs to be absolute and resolved per RFC 3986, mandates exact code-point comparison with no normalization before comparison, and defines triple terms and rdf:reifies, which give a statement its own referable identity.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Defines skos:mappingRelation, exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch and relatedMatch, with exactMatch symmetric and transitive and closeMatch deliberately non-transitive to avoid compound error across chained mappings.

sources.title: RFC 3986: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax
sources.relevance: Section 6 gives the comparison and normalization ladder and the rule that comparison minimises false negatives while strictly avoiding false positives; states that a URI provides identification only and access is neither guaranteed nor implied.

sources.title: RFC 3987: Internationalized Resource Identifiers (IRIs)
sources.relevance: Defines IRI-to-URI mapping, requires reliance on pre-character-normalized (NFC) IRIs rather than normalizing at comparison time, and repeats the graduated comparison ladder for internationalized locators.

sources.title: RFC 8288: Web Linking
sources.relevance: Defines the four-part link model (context, relation type, target, target attributes) and the anchor parameter that moves a link's context to a third resource, which is the structural precedent for an assertion about two externally owned endpoints.

sources.title: RFC 9264: Linkset: Media Types and a Link Relation Type for Link Sets
sources.relevance: Standardises third-party links, where a party publishes links about resources it does not host, and requires absolute anchors and hrefs for portability; the direct precedent for an assertion envelope whose endpoints are owned elsewhere.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines the date-time production with a mandatory seconds field and a mandatory time-offset of Z or a numeric offset, and the distinct semantics of -00:00 where UTC is known but the local offset is not.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies attribution, derivation, generation-time and primary-source terms, prov:Bundle for naming a set of provenance descriptions, and prov:alternateOf / prov:specializationOf as weaker-than-identity alternatives to sameAs.

sources.title: Describing Linked Datasets with the VoID Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines void:Linkset with void:linkPredicate, void:subjectsTarget and void:objectsTarget, establishing that a set of equivalence links declares which dataset supplies subjects and which supplies objects, i.e. explicit endpoint directionality at set level.

sources.title: Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM) specification
sources.relevance: Defines the mapping slots used here as alignment targets: subject_id, predicate_id, object_id, mapping_justification, predicate_modifier, mapping_cardinality, subject_source and object_source with version slots, curie_map, mapping_date, author_id, licence and confidence; only predicate_id and mapping_justification are required.

sources.title: A Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM)
sources.relevance: First-party description of SSSOM by its authors: argues that bare equivalence predicates obscure scope differences, that mappings need explicit justification and provenance, and acknowledges that mappings as standardised carry no context, which is the counterexample motivating explicit purpose scope here.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR R5 ConceptMap Resource
sources.relevance: Provides normative structures for canonical url plus business version and versionAlgorithm, jurisdiction and purpose, group.source/sourceVersion and group.target/targetVersion pinning, element.noMap, group.unmapped modes, target.relationship codes, and dependsOn/product attribute-value guards for conditional mappings.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines alsoKnownAs as a set of RFC 3986 URIs asserting other identifiers for the same subject, warns that its presence does not prove the assertion true, advises independent verification, and recommends not treating the pair as equivalent without a reciprocated inverse relationship; also separates subject, controller and document.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifier Resolution (DID Resolution) v1.0
sources.relevance: Defines equivalentId (a set, guaranteed logically equivalent to id, retained by requesting parties so later interactions are handled as equivalent) and canonicalId (single value, used as the primary identifier with all others treated as secondary aliases) as authority-backed contrasts to unverified alsoKnownAs claims.

sources.title: Link Relation Types registry
sources.relevance: Authoritative evidence that no 'same-as' relation type is registered, and that canonical, alternate, duplicate, describedby, via, memento and original carry narrower representation-level or provenance meanings; constrains link-shaped projections of this model.

sources.title: Identifiers for the 21st century: How to design, provision, and reuse persistent identifiers to maximize utility and impact of life science data
sources.relevance: Identifier-authority guidance: local identifiers require a prefix binding to be resolvable, prefixes should be registered against a URI pattern, published identifiers may be deprecated but must never be deleted or reassigned, and retired identifiers should continue to resolve to a tombstone.

bundles.name: Assertion Envelope
bundles.description: The alias assertion treated as an identified, versioned, weakly identified resource in its own right: what denotes it, who issued it, when it holds, for what purpose and tenant, under which jurisdiction, over which entity types, and from which citable origin it derives.
bundles.rationale: Web Linking and Linkset standardise third-party links, where a party publishes typed connections about resources it does not host; RDF 1.2 triple terms and rdf:reifies give a statement referable identity; FHIR ConceptMap and SSSOM both carry the mapping's own url, version, date, publisher, jurisdiction and purpose separately from the codes being mapped. Together these establish that the envelope is a distinct governed object, not a property of either endpoint.

layers.name: Assertion Identity and Issuance
layers.description: What identifies the assertion itself, how it depends on a host record, how it is versioned and superseded, who issued and reviewed it, and how its several distinct times are recorded.

findings.name: Assertion identifier, version and weak host-dependent identity
findings.description: The assertion is denoted by an identifier minted in a namespace disjoint from both endpoint namespaces, so it can never be mistaken for, nor substituted by, either endpoint identifier. Because this is a mixin, identity is weak and host-dependent: the addressable key is the host reference plus an assertion-local identifier, and the envelope has its own version series independent of any endpoint version. A change to any claim-bearing field is made by issuing a successor envelope that links to the one it supersedes, never by editing in place, so that consumers holding a cached copy can detect divergence.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system assertion identifier held by the adopting Dimension's assertion registry; otherwise a governed IRI minted in a Dimension-controlled namespace disjoint from both endpoint namespaces; otherwise a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The envelope identifier is never derived from, and never substitutes for, either endpoint identifier, and no date is used as an identifier.

findings.name: Issuer, authorship and the separated times of an assertion
findings.description: An alias assertion is a speech act by a named agent, and issuing one confers no authority over either endpoint. The envelope records who asserted it, who authored and who reviewed or endorsed it as distinct roles, and keeps at least three time axes apart: when the issuer asserted it, the window over which it is declared effective, and when this Dimension observed or ingested it. Conflating these makes a stale ingest indistinguishable from a fresh claim and makes retraction unverifiable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Issuer, role and time values are atomic attributes of the envelope record already declared as an artifact in this layer, and produce no separately addressable document. Agent records themselves are owned by an external party model, so only references are carried here; materialising an agent artifact locally would duplicate that model.

layers.name: Applicability, Governing Context and Provenance Locators
layers.description: The conditions under which the claim is offered and may legitimately be reused: declared purpose, tenant, jurisdiction, licence and the entity types bounding each side; plus the citable origin and derivation lineage of the assertion recorded strictly as locators.

findings.name: Purpose, tenant, jurisdiction and applicable entity/type scope
findings.description: An equivalence asserted for one purpose is not automatically valid for another. The envelope carries an explicit purpose statement, the owning tenant or adopting Dimension, the jurisdictions whose rules govern its use, the licence under which it may be redistributed, and value-set or type bounds on each side that say which classes of things the claim ranges over. This is a direct response to the standardised mapping formats that carry no context, and it means a consumer can reject an assertion as out of scope without disputing its truth.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Purpose, tenant, jurisdiction, scope bounds and licence are qualifying attributes of the envelope artifact rather than separable documents. The value sets, registers, tenant records, jurisdiction code lists and licence texts they point to are all owned by external models and registries, so this finding carries resolvable references only and deliberately materialises nothing locally.

findings.name: Provenance locators and derivation lineage of the assertion
findings.description: Provenance is recorded as locators, never as imported content. The envelope cites the set or link set it belongs to, the primary source document or dataset it came from, the prior assertion or upstream mapping set it was derived from, the activity or tool that produced it, and any issue reference where it is discussed. Set-level metadata is held once on the set descriptor and inherited by members rather than copied onto each envelope, and none of these locators is dereferenced by this model.

artifacts.name: Alias assertion set descriptor
artifacts.description: A published descriptor for a coherent set of assertions: set identity and edition, issuer and licence, the namespace binding map in force, the datasets or registers supplying source-side and target-side references and their directionality, declared default scope, and counts. Member envelopes inherit set-level metadata by reference rather than by copy.

dataset or link set description record
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system set identifier from the publishing registry; otherwise a governed set IRI in a Dimension-controlled namespace paired with an opaque edition token; otherwise a UUID or ULID. The edition token orders successive publications and carries no date-like component; the series identifier is never reused for a different endpoint pairing.

bundles.name: Endpoint Reference Boundary
bundles.description: The disciplined edge between the assertion and the two externally owned things it links: role assignment and directionality, locator form and namespace binding, version pinning and snapshot capture, the declared shape of the claim across cardinalities and conditions, and the degenerate states that must be representable rather than silently absent.
bundles.rationale: RFC 3986 and RFC 3987 fix the comparison ladder and the rule that a locator identifies without implying access; RDF 1.2 requires absolute IRIs and exact code-point comparison; VoID and Linkset establish explicit subject-side and object-side targets and third-party anchors; FHIR ConceptMap supplies source and target version pinning, noMap, unmapped modes and dependsOn guards; SSSOM supplies explicit mapping cardinality and a negation modifier. These give primary support for treating the endpoint boundary as governed structure rather than as two opaque string fields.

layers.name: Endpoint Roles and Locators
layers.description: How each side is named, which role it occupies, how its locator is written and bound to a namespace, how it is pinned to a version or snapshot, and what resolution state has been observed about it.

findings.name: Source and target roles, directionality and endpoint non-ownership
findings.description: One reference occupies the source role and the other the target, in a canonical written order that survives serialization even when the recorded predicate is symmetric, because directionality is what makes one-to-many distinguishable from many-to-one and what lets a set declare which register supplies subjects and which supplies objects. The assertion cites the authority for each endpoint rather than assuming it, and states explicitly what it does not claim: no precedence, no preferred name, no ownership, no merge. Following the strongest available guidance, a pair is not treated as equivalent on the strength of a single unreciprocated claim.

The endpoint records and the authority registers they point at are owned by external models; materialising either here would import records this model is explicitly forbidden to own, so only role-bearing references are held inline.

findings.name: Locator form, namespace binding and comparison discipline
findings.description: Each endpoint locator is recorded in a declared form: an absolute IRI, a compact prefixed form expandable through a published binding map, or a local code paired with an explicit scheme. Comparison is not a free choice: RDF-facing use requires exact code-point comparison of absolute IRIs with no normalization beforehand, while URI and IRI guidance defines a graduated ladder whose whole design principle is to minimise false negatives while strictly avoiding false positives. The envelope therefore records which normalization level was applied, keeps character data in Normalization Form C, states how percent-encoding and fragment components were handled, and flags locators declared opaque so that no meaning is parsed out of their internal structure.

artifacts.name: Endpoint namespace and prefix binding map
artifacts.description: The published map from prefix tokens to IRI patterns used to expand compact endpoint locators, together with its edition and the authority that publishes each binding. It is the only sanctioned way a compact locator becomes comparable, and a change to a binding changes the meaning of every stored assertion that cites it.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system identifier for the binding map issued by its publishing registry; otherwise a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID. Individual prefix tokens are keys within the map and are never identifiers of the map itself, and the map identifier is never an endpoint identifier.

findings.name: Version pins, composite keys, snapshots and endpoint resolution status
findings.description: An endpoint reference is either pinned to a stated version of its source register or left to float to whatever is current, and the difference must be explicit because a floating reference can silently change the claim. Where an endpoint is identified by more than one field, the composite key is recorded as structured parts, not concatenated into an unparseable string. The envelope distinguishes an immutable snapshot capture, which fixes what was seen, from a live reference, which does not, and it records the last observed resolution status with the time of that observation, treating resolution as an observation made elsewhere rather than an act performed here.

artifacts.name: Endpoint reference snapshot
artifacts.description: An immutable capture of what an endpoint reference presented at pin time: the locator, the version token in force, the composite key parts and a content digest of the captured representation. It exists so that a claim remains interpretable after the live endpoint changes, and it is a capture of a reference, not a copy of the endpoint's record content beyond what is needed to fix identity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Content digest of the captured reference bound to the endpoint's authoritative master-system identifier and the capture sequence; otherwise a governed snapshot IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID. The snapshot identifier never replaces the endpoint's own identifier and is never used as the assertion identifier.

layers.name: Assertion Shape: Cardinality, Membership and Conditions
layers.description: How the claim's arity, membership semantics, ordering and applicability guards are made explicit on the envelope instead of being inferred from repeated entries.

findings.name: Cardinality, ordered membership and conditional applicability
findings.description: Cardinality is declared, not inferred. A bare two-column mapping cannot distinguish a genuine one-to-many claim from several independent one-to-one claims, so the envelope carries an explicit cardinality declaration covering one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many, together with a combination rule stating whether a multi-member side is a union, a set of alternatives or a ranked preference order, and an explicit rank where order matters. Conditional mappings are expressed as attribute-value guards naming externally defined attributes, with any attributes produced by applying the mapping recorded separately. This model declares the guards; evaluating them at runtime is done elsewhere.

questions.text: What cardinality does this assertion declare, and is that declaration explicit or merely implied by repeated entries?
answer_data: Cardinality code (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, many-to-many)
Whether the declaration is asserted or derived
Count of members on each side

questions.text: When several targets are asserted for one source, is the member set a union, a list of alternatives or a ranked preference?
answer_data: Combination rule code
Member list per side
Tie-breaking rule where ranks collide

questions.text: Which conditions must hold for the assertion to apply, and how are they expressed as attribute-value guards?
answer_data: Condition attribute references
Required values or bounding value sets per condition
Statement that guard evaluation is performed by an external evaluator

questions.text: How is a member's rank within a multi-member side recorded so that it survives serialization?
answer_data: Explicit rank value per member
Rule forbidding reliance on serialization order
Declared behaviour when ranks are absent

questions.text: Which combination of source and target members forms the smallest independently assertable unit?
answer_data: Definition of the atomic assertable unit
Rule for splitting a multi-member claim into units
Effect of splitting on the declared cardinality

data_elements.name: cardinality_declaration
data_elements.description: Explicit code declaring the arity of the claim across both sides.

data_elements.name: member_combination_rule
data_elements.description: Code stating whether a multi-member side is a union, a set of alternatives or a ranked preference order.

data_elements.name: member_rank
data_elements.description: Explicit rank of a member within its side, recorded so ordering does not depend on serialization order.

data_elements.name: applicability_condition
data_elements.description: Attribute-value guard that must hold for the assertion to apply, expressed against externally defined attributes.

data_elements.name: condition_attribute_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to the external definition of an attribute named in a guard; the definition is not copied here.

data_elements.name: produced_attribute
data_elements.description: Attribute-value pair recorded as a stated consequence of applying the mapping, distinct from a guard.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Cardinality, membership, ordering and guards are structural fields of the envelope record already declared as an artifact, and they gain nothing from a separate document. The attribute definitions named in guards are owned by external terminology and schema models, and guard evaluation belongs to a runtime evaluator outside this boundary, so this finding declares shape as inline data and references those definitions only.

layers.name: Degenerate, Conflicting and Malformed References
layers.description: The states that a two-column mapping cannot represent: absence versus explicit unknown versus explicit denial, dangling and unresolved endpoints, malformed references, self links, duplicate envelopes and conflicting pins.

findings.name: Absence, explicit unknown, explicit not-same, dangling endpoints, self links, duplicates and conflicts
findings.description: Three states must be kept apart and none may be inferred from silence: no assertion exists, an endpoint is explicitly recorded as unknown, and equivalence is explicitly denied. Explicit denial is a positive claim with its own justification and issuer, expressible either through an inequality predicate or a negation modifier on the predicate slot, and it must never degrade into an absent or weak claim. Alongside these, the envelope represents dangling and unresolved endpoints, malformed or unresolvable relative references, self links where both sides normalize to the same locator, structurally identical duplicate envelopes, and conflicts where two assertions about the same pair pin different endpoint versions or make opposing claims. Conflicts are recorded and linked here; adjudicating, remediating, retracting or enforcing them is done elsewhere.

questions.text: How does the record distinguish a missing endpoint from an endpoint explicitly recorded as unknown?
answer_data: Presence state code (present, absent, explicitly unknown)
Rule that absence is never read as a claim
Reason code for a declared unknown

questions.text: How is an explicit denial of equivalence recorded so that it cannot be read as a weak or absent claim?
answer_data: Negation modifier or inequality predicate reference
Justification and issuer for the denial
Statement that a denial carries the same standing as a positive claim

questions.text: What is recorded when an endpoint locator is malformed or is a relative reference that cannot be resolved to an absolute form?
answer_data: Malformed-reference note with the offending value preserved verbatim
Missing base reference indication
Quarantine state preventing the envelope from being treated as a live claim

questions.text: How is a self link, where both sides normalize to the same locator, detected and flagged?
answer_data: Self-link flag
Normalization level at which the collision was found
Declared handling (retain as flagged, or reject at creation)

questions.text: When two assertions about the same pair pin different endpoint versions or make opposing claims, how is the conflict recorded without being resolved here?
answer_data: Conflicts-with references between envelope identifiers
Conflict type code (version divergence, opposing claim, duplicate)
Reference to the external model that adjudicates and enforces resolution

data_elements.name: endpoint_presence_state
data_elements.description: Code per side distinguishing a present endpoint, an absent one and one explicitly recorded as unknown.

data_elements.name: negation_modifier
data_elements.description: Modifier or inequality predicate reference recording that equivalence is explicitly denied rather than merely unasserted.

data_elements.name: malformed_reference_note
data_elements.description: Record of a syntactically invalid or unresolvable relative locator, preserving the offending value verbatim.

data_elements.name: self_link_flag
data_elements.description: Flag set when both sides normalize to the same locator at the declared normalization level.

data_elements.name: duplicate_of_ref
data_elements.description: Reference to a structurally identical envelope within the same declared scope, linked rather than silently merged.

data_elements.name: conflicts_with_ref
data_elements.description: References to envelopes that make opposing claims or pin divergent endpoint versions for the same pair.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Every item here is a state code, flag or link recorded on the envelope record itself, so no separate document is warranted. Materialising an exception or conflict register as an artifact would drift into the audit-record and enforcement semantics that belong to the audit and authorization models, so these anomalies are held strictly as inline attributes and cross-references between envelope identifiers.

functions.name: Compose alias assertion envelope
functions.description: Assemble a new assertion envelope from two role-bearing endpoint references, an issuer, a declared purpose scope and a host record, minting an assertion identifier in a namespace disjoint from both endpoint namespaces.
inputs: Purpose, tenant, jurisdiction and scope declaration
outputs: Identified alias assertion envelope record
Assertion identifier and initial envelope version
preconditions: Both endpoint locators are absolute or expandable through a published namespace binding, or a presence state of absent or explicitly unknown is declared
An issuer is named and an assertion time with an explicit offset is supplied
The host record exists and its retention scope is known
effects: Creates a new envelope with its own identifier and version series
Records role order, purpose scope and tenant on the envelope
Creates, renames or modifies nothing at either endpoint and reserves no endpoint identifier

functions.name: Bind and normalize an endpoint locator
functions.description: Expand a compact or local endpoint reference into an absolute locator using a cited namespace binding, and record the normalization level applied so that comparison behaviour is reproducible.
inputs: Raw endpoint locator with its declared form
Namespace or prefix binding map reference and edition

Recorded normalization level and locator form code
Namespace binding reference used for expansion

A relative reference is accompanied by an explicit base reference, otherwise it is routed to the malformed-reference path
Character data is in Normalization Form C before comparison

Records the normalization level so a later consumer can reproduce or reject the comparison
Mints, alters or reassigns no endpoint identifier and edits no binding map owned by another authority

Composite keys are recorded as named parts rather than concatenated strings

Makes a floating reference explicit where no pin is available
Copies no endpoint attributes beyond the locator, key parts, version token and digest

functions.name: Record an endpoint resolution observation

Performs no dereference, no redirect, no retry and no repair of any endpoint

The issuer is authorised under the adopting Dimension's governance for this tenant

composition.purpose: Specializes the parent reference model for the single case of an asserted equivalence between two references. Identifier syntax, scheme and namespace registration, allocation, non-reuse guarantees, generic authority machinery and resolution execution remain wholly with the parent and are used by reference here.

composition.target: Host record adopting the alias mixin
composition.purpose: The envelope attaches to a host record that supplies its weak identity context, tenancy and retention scope. The host owns its own lifecycle and disposition; the mixin contributes only the assertion fields.

composition.target: Endpoint entity and record models at each side
composition.purpose: Carries role-bearing locators, version pins, composite key parts, snapshot digests and recorded resolution observations for records owned elsewhere. Endpoint attributes, descriptions, classifications and lifecycles are never imported or mutated here.

composition.target: Identifier issuing and registration authority model
composition.purpose: Cites the authority governing each endpoint namespace, its version tokens, deprecation notices and non-reuse guarantees. Allocation, minting, retirement and tombstoning of endpoint identifiers are executed entirely by that authority.

composition.target: Relation classification and semantic predicate vocabularies
composition.purpose: Binds the envelope's predicate slot to externally defined terms (owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom, the SKOS mapping properties, ConceptMap relationship codes). Term definitions, sub-property hierarchies and entailment consequences stay in those vocabularies; only the term reference and an optional negation modifier are carried here.

composition.target: Formal equivalence closure and reasoning model
composition.purpose: Supplies asserted pairs as input to entailment and transitive-closure computation. This model neither computes, materialises nor stores closure results, and forbids local chaining of assertions because the mapping predicates differ in transitivity.

Consumes candidate evidence produced by matching engines and records only the justification locator, tool reference and creator-supplied confidence. Blocking, similarity computation, thresholding and engine execution remain outside.

composition.target: Master data merge and survivorship model
composition.purpose: Provides asserted pairs that a merge process may consume. Golden-record construction, survivorship rules, redirect execution and any physical consolidation of endpoint records are owned entirely by that model.

Maps envelope fields onto SSSOM mapping and mapping-set slots for interchange, noting that SSSOM requires only predicate_id and mapping_justification while this model additionally requires bound endpoint references or an explicit presence state. Alignment is declared; conformance is not claimed without a published validation report.

composition.target: HL7 FHIR R5 ConceptMap exchange profile
composition.purpose: Aligns endpoint scoping, source and target version pinning, no-map and unmapped handling, and dependsOn condition guards with ConceptMap structures for healthcare interchange, without adopting FHIR's terminology-service behaviour.

composition.target: Link set and dataset description profiles
composition.purpose: Aligns the assertion set descriptor with third-party link set documents and dataset link descriptions, including explicit subject-side and object-side targets and absolute anchors, so that assertion sets are publishable without a bespoke format.

Expresses issuance, attribution, derivation and primary-source citation of the assertion using PROV terms, and uses named provenance bundles for set-level attribution. Provenance record storage and provenance-of-provenance remain external.
Supplies tenant, jurisdiction, purpose and licence attributes as decision inputs. Policy evaluation, decision records and enforcement are owned there; this model makes and stores no access decision.

Receives creation, supersession, retraction and tombstoning events carrying the assertion identifier, issuer, event time and observation time. Audit-record structure, retention, integrity and tamper evidence are owned there; this model stores no audit trail.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names a single accountable owner for the alias assertion package and records that owner reference on every assertion set descriptor it publishes.

The owner publishes the namespace and prefix binding map used to expand compact endpoint locators and keeps it resolvable for at least as long as any assertion citing it remains readable, because a binding change silently changes the meaning of stored assertions.
The owner declares, per tenant, which endpoint authorities are recognised, the default reference mode (snapshot or live) and the default normalization level used for locator comparison.

The owner records in the package manifest that this package holds no allocation, naming, merge, redirect, reasoning-closure, authorization or audit authority, and names the model that owns each of those.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint assertion identifiers, set identifiers, snapshot identifiers and binding-map identifiers in Dimension-controlled namespaces that are provably disjoint from every endpoint namespace, so no local identifier can ever be mistaken for, or silently substituted by, an endpoint identifier. Treat all endpoint namespaces as read-only foreign namespaces: never mint into them, never rewrite a stored locator in place, and expand compact forms only through a cited, versioned binding map. Where a locator is declared opaque, forbid consumers from parsing structure out of it.
registry_links: The adopting Dimension's assertion registry acts as master system for assertion, set and snapshot identifiers.
The published namespace and prefix binding registry that resolves compact endpoint locators to absolute IRI patterns.
The IANA Link Relation Types registry for any registered relation token used in a link-shaped projection; note that no 'same-as' relation type is registered, so extension relation URIs are required.
The registration authority registers governing each endpoint namespace, cited by locator only and never mirrored locally.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form records both endpoints as absolute IRIs together with the normalization level applied. Simple string comparison is the default, and any higher normalization level must be recorded explicitly, because comparison is designed to minimise false negatives while strictly avoiding false positives.
Compact and local forms are canonicalized by expansion against the cited binding map and edition; the original form may be retained for display but is never the comparison key.

Character data is stored pre-normalized in Unicode Normalization Form C, and no further normalization is applied at comparison time, so that exact code-point comparison remains available to RDF-facing consumers.

Role order is canonical: the source-role reference is written first and the target second, even where the recorded predicate names a symmetric term, so that one-to-many and many-to-one remain distinguishable.
Cardinality, combination rule and member ranks are written explicitly and are never left to be inferred from repetition or serialization order.
patch_rules: Claim-bearing fields (endpoint locators, role order, predicate slot and negation modifier, version pins, reference mode, cardinality and condition guards) are immutable once issued; any change requires a successor envelope citing the one it supersedes.
Non-claim metadata (comments, see-also links, display labels) and newly observed resolution status may be patched in place, always accompanied by a new observation timestamp.
A patch never edits an endpoint record, never rewrites a binding map owned by another authority, and never modifies a captured snapshot.
A retraction is recorded as a patch to lifecycle state plus a retraction reason and issuer; it never removes the retracted claim from the record.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional envelope fields is backward compatible. Changing the meaning of an existing field, narrowing an enumeration or making an optional field required is a breaking change that requires a new envelope schema version.
Consumers must ignore unknown envelope fields and must never infer equivalence, denial or applicability from the absence of a field.
External profile alignments are declared with the profile name and version they target; conformance is claimed only where a published validation report exists.
A change to a namespace binding that alters how a stored compact locator expands is treated as breaking for every assertion citing that binding, and is announced rather than applied silently.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the artifact: for an assertion envelope, set descriptor, snapshot or binding map, the identifier held by the adopting Dimension's assertion registry or the artifact's publishing registry.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in a Dimension-controlled namespace that is provably disjoint from every endpoint namespace, used where no master-system identifier exists.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, recorded as opaque, used only where neither a master-system identifier nor a governed IRI is available.
A content digest may accompany but never replace an identifier; a date, a version token, an edition token or an endpoint identifier is never an identifier for a local artifact.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All times are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time values that include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or 'Z'; '-00:00' is used only where UTC is known but the local offset is not, and is not treated as equivalent to 'Z'. Event time (when the issuer asserted, made effective, superseded or retracted the claim) is recorded in fields separate from observation or ingestion time (when this Dimension observed an endpoint resolution outcome or ingested the assertion), and the two are never collapsed into a single field or defaulted from each other.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely assertion set descriptors and endpoint reference snapshots, keep one stable series identifier plus a monotonically increasing opaque edition or capture token. The token carries no date-like component and embeds no endpoint identifier, ordering is declared by an explicit version algorithm rather than inferred from lexical form, and a series identifier is never reused for a different set or a different endpoint.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest and the identifier of the issuing agent. Snapshots are immutable once captured; any divergence between a snapshot digest and a live endpoint is recorded as a new observation with its own observation time rather than silently repaired, and no artifact is rewritten in place to conceal a divergence. Integrity here is limited to self-describing digests and issuer attribution: tamper-evident logging is owned by the audit model.

policies: An alias assertion is a claim, not proof. No consumer may treat two endpoints as equivalent solely because an assertion exists; reciprocity or independent verification is required before equivalence is acted upon, and the assurance level (unverified third-party claim versus authority-guaranteed equivalence) is always recorded.
This model never allocates, mints, renames, merges, redirects, retires or deletes an endpoint identifier or record. It cites them and nothing more.

Absence of an assertion is not a claim. An explicit unknown and an explicit denial of equivalence are first-class, separately recorded states, and a denial carries the same standing and provenance requirements as a positive claim.
Cardinality, membership and ordering are declared explicitly on the envelope and are never left to be inferred from repeated rows or serialization order.

Transitive chaining of assertions is prohibited within this model. Closure, where computed at all, is produced by the external reasoning model under its own rules, because the available mapping predicates differ in transitivity and chaining compounds error.
A mapping asserted under one declared purpose scope is not valid under another; consumers must check scope before use, and may reject an assertion as out of scope without disputing its truth.

read: Read an envelope by its own assertion identifier, or list envelopes filtered by endpoint locator, tenant, purpose scope, predicate slot or set membership.
Reading an envelope never dereferences an endpoint; resolution state is read only from recorded observations together with their observation times.
Set-level metadata is read through the set descriptor and inherited by reference; it is not duplicated onto member envelopes.
Every read returns the assertion identifier, issuer, assertion time and declared purpose scope alongside the claim, so a claim is never consumed anonymously or out of context.
create: Create an envelope only with both role-bearing references bound to absolute form, or with an explicit absent or unknown presence state, plus a named issuer, an assertion time with an explicit offset, and a declared purpose scope and tenant.
Creation mints an assertion identifier in a Dimension namespace disjoint from both endpoint namespaces, and must not mint, reserve or alter any endpoint identifier.
A new envelope is compared against existing envelopes within the same declared scope for structural duplicates and self links, and duplicates are linked rather than silently merged or discarded.
An envelope carrying a malformed or unresolvable relative locator is created in a quarantine state and is not treated as a live claim.
update: Claim-bearing fields are immutable; every change to them is made by issuing a superseding envelope that cites the one it supersedes and leaves the prior envelope intact.
Non-claim metadata and newly observed endpoint resolution status may be updated in place, always accompanied by a new observation timestamp with an explicit offset.
Updates never write into an endpoint record, a binding map owned by another authority, or a captured snapshot.
Changing lifecycle state to disputed, superseded or retracted requires an issuer reference and a reason code, and never erases the prior claim.
delete: Envelopes are not hard-deleted by default. An assertion that ceases to hold is retracted or superseded and retained as a tombstone that preserves its identifier, issuer, assertion time, prior claim and retraction reason, so that consumers who cached it can detect the change.

A tombstoned assertion identifier is never reused for a different endpoint pair, and continues to resolve to its tombstone rather than returning nothing, following the identifier guidance that published identifiers may be deprecated but must never be deleted or reassigned.

Retention classes, legal-hold and erasure obligations for envelopes are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy policy, which owns execution. This model records only the retention class, the disposition decision reference and the resulting tombstone state; where erasure of an assertion linking identifiers of a natural person is ordered, that policy executes it and this model records that a tombstone with claim content redacted remains.

Deleting or purging an endpoint record is executed by the endpoint's owning model and its authority; purging an audit entry about an assertion is executed by the audit model. Neither is performed here, and neither may be inferred from the deletion of an envelope.
Deleting an envelope never propagates to either endpoint, never triggers a merge or unmerge, and never removes a snapshot that other assertions still cite.

roles.name: Assertion issuer
responsibilities: State the claim and accept accountability for it
Declare the purpose scope, tenant and jurisdiction under which it is offered
Record the justification locator and, where used, the negation modifier for an explicit denial
Authorise supersession or retraction of assertions they issued

roles.name: Endpoint authority liaison
responsibilities: Confirm which system is authoritative for each endpoint namespace
Supply version tokens, deprecation notices and tombstone locators from that authority
Ensure no allocation, renaming or retirement decision is delegated to this model

roles.name: Namespace and binding steward
responsibilities: Publish and keep resolvable the prefix and namespace binding map with its edition
Record binding changes as new editions rather than edits, and announce them as breaking for citing assertions
Maintain the disjointness guarantee between local and endpoint namespaces

roles.name: Assertion set curator
responsibilities: Maintain set descriptors and their editions, and the inheritance of set-level metadata
Run structural validation for self links, duplicates, malformed references and conflicting pins
Link conflicting envelopes for downstream adjudication without resolving the conflict
Publish assertion sets in the agreed exchange profiles with their profile versions

roles.name: Dimension data owner
responsibilities: Approve tenancy, jurisdiction and licence declarations
Own the retention, disposition and privacy policy applied to envelopes and snapshots
Approve which endpoint authorities are recognised and the default reference and normalization modes
Confirm that no allocation, merge, closure, authorization or audit authority is exercised by this package

access.default_rule: Envelope structure and endpoint locators are readable by any agent permitted to read the host record, and every read discloses the assertion identifier, issuer, assertion time and declared purpose scope with the claim, so that no claim is consumed as an anonymous fact.
exceptions: Assertions whose endpoints identify natural persons are restricted to the tenant's authorised purpose scope, because linking two identifiers of a person is itself personal data even when neither endpoint record is disclosed.

Snapshot artifacts and set descriptors may carry licensed third-party material and inherit the endpoint publisher's terms; redistribution follows the recorded licence reference rather than the default rule.
Draft, quarantined or disputed envelopes are withheld from downstream propagation until an issuer, an assertion time and a justification locator are present.
Assertion sets under jurisdictional restriction are readable only within the declared jurisdictions recorded on the envelope.
All access decisions are made and enforced by the external authorization model; this model exposes scope, tenant, jurisdiction and licence attributes as decision inputs and enforces nothing itself.
audit_requirements: Creation, supersession, retraction and tombstoning of an envelope emit events carrying the assertion identifier, issuer, event time and observation time, for capture by the external audit model.
Changes to a namespace binding map that alter how a stored compact locator expands are announced as events, because they change the meaning of assertions already recorded.
Bulk import or export of assertion sets emits a set-level event citing the set identifier, edition and licence.

This model stores no audit trail and offers no retention, completeness or tamper-evidence guarantee over audit records; record structure, retention and integrity are owned entirely by the audit model.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve the Specification URL before interpreting any stored envelope, regardless of whether storage is a document store, a graph, a database or a message interface.

Read the specification, then the namespace and prefix binding map with its edition, then the assertion set descriptor, then individual envelopes, so that every compact locator is expandable before any claim is interpreted.

Read the composition links and boundary notes before acting on a claim, so that predicate semantics, closure, matching, merge, authorization and audit are sought from their owning models rather than assumed here.
Never dereference an endpoint locator as part of bootstrap; endpoint resolution is governed by the referenced reference and resolution model and enters this model only as a recorded observation.

coverage.claim: The alias / same-as mapping is modelled as an identified, versioned, weakly host-dependent assertion envelope over two externally owned references, grounded in primary W3C RDF, OWL, SKOS, PROV and DID specifications, IETF URI, IRI, Web Linking, Linkset and timestamp standards, the IANA link relation registry, HL7 FHIR R5 ConceptMap and the SSSOM mapping profile. Predicate vocabulary definition, entailment closure, matching, merge, redirect execution, identifier allocation, authorization and audit are bounded out to named neighbouring models and cited rather than reproduced.

checklist.notes: The assertion carries its own identifier in a namespace disjoint from both endpoints, with an explicit structural key for duplicate detection, and weak host-dependent addressability. Backed by RDF 1.2 triple-term and reification semantics, ConceptMap url plus identifier plus version, and the identifier-authority rule that identifiers are never reassigned.

Envelope versioning, supersession, retraction and tombstoning are owned locally with claim-bearing fields immutable. Endpoint lifecycle is explicitly excluded and delegated to the endpoint authority; the model records deprecation notices rather than issuing them.

Source and target roles, canonical order, directionality versus symmetry, reciprocity, conflicts-with and duplicate-of links, and the predicate slot bound to external vocabularies. Set-level subject-side and object-side targets follow the Linkset and VoID pattern.

Assertion time, effective window and observation or ingestion time are separate fields with RFC 3339 formatting including seconds and an explicit offset. Endpoint version pins and snapshot capture give temporal fixity to references without freezing endpoint content.

Primary-source locator, derivation lineage, producing activity or tool, issue locators, set membership and inherited set metadata, all recorded as resolvable locators aligned to PROV terms and SSSOM provenance slots, with no imported endpoint content.

Issuer, author and reviewer roles are distinct; endpoint non-ownership is an explicit recorded declaration; tenant and Dimension ownership of the assertion instance is required. Endpoint authority is cited, never assumed.

Structural validation covers locator absoluteness and normalization level, self links, duplicates within scope, malformed and relative references, presence-state completeness and reciprocity checks. Runtime evaluation of condition guards is explicitly external.

Default read rule ties envelope visibility to the host record and always discloses issuer and scope. Exceptions cover natural-person endpoints, licensed third-party material, quarantined or disputed envelopes and jurisdictional restriction; decisions and enforcement are delegated.

Tombstone-by-default with identifier non-reuse and continued resolution to the tombstone; retention class and disposition decision reference recorded locally while the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy policy owns execution. Endpoint deletion and audit purging are explicitly outside.

Alignments declared to SSSOM, FHIR R5 ConceptMap, Linkset and VoID, plus the finding that no 'same-as' link relation is registered with IANA so extension relation URIs are required. Conformance is claimed only against a published validation report.

One-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many are declared explicitly with a combination rule and per-member ranks, following SSSOM mapping cardinality and ConceptMap group and element structure, so arity is never inferred from repeated rows.
Attribute-value guards and produced attributes follow ConceptMap dependsOn and product, with attribute definitions referenced externally and evaluation delegated to a runtime evaluator.
Absence, explicit unknown and explicit denial are three distinct recorded states, supported by OWL individual inequality, the SSSOM negation modifier and ConceptMap noMap and unmapped modes.

Resolution status and its observation time are recorded from externally produced observations, with retired-and-tombstoned distinguished from never-existed. Dereference, redirect and repair are excluded because a URI provides identification only.

No primary standard defines a comparable, interoperable confidence scale for equivalence assertions. SSSOM's confidence slot is an unnormalised creator estimate between 0.0 and 1.0 with no calibration semantics, so the model carries confidence as an issuer-scoped opaque value and marks a comparable scale as an evidence gap rather than presenting one as canonical.

Authentication, key management, signature verification and transport security are owned by the adopting Dimension's security and authorization models. This model records issuer attribution and content digests only, and asserts no cryptographic guarantee.

known_omissions: No definition of predicate vocabulary terms or their entailments; owl:sameAs, owl:differentFrom, the SKOS mapping properties and ConceptMap relationship codes are cited as external vocabularies and are not redefined, extended or reinterpreted here.

No algorithm for selecting a preferred or canonical endpoint from an equivalence group; canonical selection is left to the endpoint authority, following the DID Resolution pattern in which the method specification, not a third-party claim, guarantees a canonical identifier.

No modelling of link discovery, blocking keys, similarity functions or scoring thresholds; the model records the resulting justification locator and confidence but not the computation that produced them.

No single mandated encoding for the assertion; reification with triple terms, named graphs, tabular mapping rows and link set documents are all treated as projections of the same semantics, and their trade-offs are not adjudicated.
No treatment of commercial or contractual settlement for redistributing third-party mapping sets beyond a licence reference on the envelope and set descriptor.

No cross-tenant reconciliation procedure for the case where two tenants hold contradictory assertions about the same pair under different purpose scopes; the conflict is representable but adjudication is delegated.
conflicts: skos:exactMatch is symmetric and transitive but is explicitly a mapping property between concepts, not owl:sameAs, whose consequences propagate to every property of the individuals. Any single 'same-as' field that does not record which vocabulary is meant changes entailments when the data is consumed by a reasoner.

skos:closeMatch is deliberately non-transitive to avoid compound error across chained mappings while skos:exactMatch is transitive. A model that stores one flat equivalence flag cannot preserve this distinction, which is why chaining is prohibited locally and the predicate term is always named.

RDF 1.2 requires exact code-point comparison of IRIs with no normalization performed before comparison, whereas RFC 3986 and RFC 3987 define a graduated normalization ladder. Storing a normalized locator without recording the level applied makes it impossible to reproduce either behaviour, so the normalization level is a required part of the record rather than an implementation detail.

The IANA Link Relation Types registry contains no 'same-as' relation. 'canonical' designates a preferred version of a resource, 'duplicate' designates byte-for-byte identical representations and 'alternate' designates a substitute; none of these is identity equivalence, so link-shaped projections must use extension relation URIs and must not borrow these tokens.

SSSOM requires only predicate_id and mapping_justification, leaving subject_id and object_id optional, which permits records this model treats as incomplete envelopes. The divergence is recorded as an alignment note rather than reconciled, and importing such records produces envelopes in a quarantine or explicit-unknown state.

DID Core states that the presence of an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove it true and advises against treating identifiers as equivalent without a reciprocated inverse relationship, whereas DID Resolution requires a conforming method to guarantee that equivalentId and canonicalId are logically equivalent to the id. Structurally similar fields therefore span very different assurance levels, so assurance level is recorded explicitly on every assertion.

The SSSOM authors acknowledge that mappings as standardised carry no context and are designed to be universally applicable, while ConceptMap scopes a mapping by purpose, jurisdiction and value set. This model follows the scoped reading and treats context-free mappings as under-specified, which is a deliberate divergence from the simpler profile.
regional_assumptions: Jurisdiction is modelled as a declared code list on the envelope and no specific legal regime is assumed. Where endpoints identify natural persons, a GDPR-style purpose-limitation reading is taken as the stricter default for the access exception, and adopting Dimensions under other regimes may relax it by explicit declaration.

Erasure and legal-hold semantics vary by regime; the model records a retention class and disposition decision reference and leaves execution to the adopting Dimension, so a jurisdiction requiring full erasure rather than tombstoning must be handled by that policy, not by this model.
Healthcare-facing alignment assumes HL7 FHIR R5 terminology practice, which is normative in that sector but is not a general-purpose assumption outside it.

Language, script and bidirectional handling of display labels follows IRI internationalization guidance; locale-specific collation, transliteration equivalence and script-variant matching are not assumed and are not treated as evidence of sameness.

Identifier-authority guidance drawn from life-science practice generalises well on non-reuse and tombstoning, but its prefix-registry assumptions may not hold in sectors without a shared prefix registry, in which case the Dimension's own binding map is the sole authority.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether this model should own an endpoint resolution or dereference function. Rejected: RFC 3986 states that a URI provides identification only and that access is neither guaranteed nor implied, and resolution execution belongs to the referenced reference and resolution model. The model therefore records externally produced resolution observations with their observation times and performs no dereference, redirect or repair.

Tested whether a transitive-closure or 'merge equivalent identifiers' function could be justified locally. Rejected on two independent grounds: closure is an entailment consequence owned by the reasoning model and the available predicates differ in transitivity, and merge with survivorship is owned by the master-data model. Both were moved to composition links and out_of_scope.

Tested whether 'same-as' could be projected onto a registered IANA link relation type. The registry has no such relation, and 'canonical', 'duplicate' and 'alternate' address representation preference, byte-identity and substitution respectively. The attractive shortcut was rejected and extension relation URIs are required instead.

Tested whether the envelope could key itself on one of the endpoint identifiers, which would simplify lookup. Rejected because it makes the assertion indistinguishable from the endpoint, silently asserts precedence for one side, and would collide with the endpoint authority's non-reuse guarantees. Namespace disjointness became an explicit governance requirement.

Tested whether cardinality could be left implicit in repeated rows, as in common two-column mapping files. Rejected because a genuine one-to-many claim then becomes indistinguishable from several independent one-to-one claims, and because the ranked-preference case cannot be recovered from serialization order.

Tested whether an exception or conflict register should be a local artifact. Rejected because a durable register of what went wrong, who saw it and when drifts into audit-record and enforcement semantics owned elsewhere; anomalies are held as inline state codes and cross-references between envelope identifiers instead.

Searched for a primary standard defining a comparable, calibrated confidence scale for equivalence assertions and found none. Rather than inventing a scale, confidence is carried as an issuer-scoped opaque value and the absence of a comparable scale is recorded as a checklist gap.

Tested whether the model could declare conformance to SSSOM or ConceptMap on the strength of field-level correspondence. Rejected: the required-field sets differ and no validation report exists, so both are recorded as declared alignments with named profile versions rather than conformance claims.
